newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria may delay CA sale to end government row.
newsitem.headline: Austria may delay CA sale to end government row.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima, at pains to halt a damaging row that could topple the coalition government, said he was prepared to delay the sale of second biggest bank Creditanstalt until next year.

"If possible we will decide this month -- without endangering the coalition. But if there is a reason not to decide before year-end, then we won't do it," Klima, a Social Democrat, told the current affairs magazine Profil in an interview to be published on Monday.
"I am ready to do a lot of things, including reopen the bidding so that people can alter their bids without drawing in new partners," Klima added.
He had insisted he wanted to complete Europe's longest running privatisation by the end of 1996, closing what has become an embarrassing chapter for Austria.

Klima, the third finance minister to attempt the sale in the past six years, appeared to be on track to meet his target until market leader Bank Austria entered the fray shortly before the December 16 deadline for bids.

"Socialist" Bank Austria's offer for conservative stronghold Creditanstalt split the coalition of Social Democrats and rightist People's Party down the middle, raising the spectre of a repeat of last year's snap elections.

The People's Party, the junior coalition partner, has threatened Klima with an emergency session of parliament and a vote of no-confidence if he sells the state's 70 percent of voting shares to Bank Austria.
A group led by Italian-controlled insurer EA-Generali, the conservatives' favoured choice, has said it will take the matter to the European Union if its bid fails.

Klima says his hands are tied by EU regulations that require him to choose the best bidder. Bank Austria has reportedly put up some 16 billion schillings ($1.5 billion) for the state's holding, worth about 14.5 billion at market prices.

Two rival bids from the EA-Generali group, which includes savings bank Die Erste Oesterriechische SparCasse Bank (First Austrian), Germany's Commerzbank and Italy's Banca Commerciale Italiana, and from entrepreneur Karl Wlaschek lag by more than one billion.
Economy Minister Johann Farnleitner, a member of the People's Party, welcomed Klima's conciliatory remarks.
"I am willing to find a solution. I have the feeling there is a genuine will to find a solution that would be good for the country," he told Kurier newspaper.
The move towards a reconciliation coincided with the release of an opinion poll on Sunday that showed both the Social Democrats and People's Party would fare badly if an election were called today.
According to the survey by Linz-based research institute, Market, support for the Social Democrats has slipped to 32 percent from 38 percent in last year's general election.

The People's Party slumped to third place behind Joerg Haider's far-right Freedom Party. The People's Party had 26 percent support, down from 28, while the Freedom Party advanced to 27 percent from 22.
